Diagnosing how well a model classifies ties

Source: R/diagnose_confusion.R, R/report_diagnose.R
diagnose_confusion.Rd

diagnose_confusion() compares the ties that a model of a binary outcome predicts with the ties that were observed. It has a method for a netreg from estimate_mrqap(): a logistic model, or a linear model of a 0/1 outcome, read as a linear probability model.

  • The probabilistic confusion matrix draws each tie from its predicted probability, times times, and gives the mean count of each cell with a 95% interval, so it shows how uncertain the classification is.

  • The metrics are the means over those draws: the accuracy, the sensitivity (the share of observed ties that are predicted), the specificity (the share of observed non-ties that are predicted), the precision (the share of predicted ties that are observed), and F1.

  • The confusion matrix at threshold classifies each dyad as a tie where its predicted probability is at least threshold.

  • The ROC curve gives the true positive rate against the false positive rate at every threshold, and the AUC is the area under it: the probability that an observed tie has a higher predicted probability than an observed non-tie.

print() shows the matrix, tidy() gives the ROC curve, and glance() gives the metrics in one row, after {broom}. {autograph} plots it.

Usage

diagnose_confusion(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
diagnose_confusion(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netreg_glm'
diagnose_confusion(x, threshold = 0.5, times = 1000, control = list(), ...)

# S3 method for class 'netreg_lm'
diagnose_confusion(x, threshold = 0.5, times = 1000, control = list(), ...)

# S3 method for class 'diagnose_confusion'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'diagnose_confusion'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'diagnose_confusion'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A netreg of a binary outcome, from estimate_mrqap(). For print(), tidy(), and glance(), the result of diagnose_confusion().

...

Not used.

threshold

The predicted probability at or above which a dyad is classified as a tie.

times

The number of draws of the probabilistic confusion matrix.

control

A list with a seed, as for control_mrqap(). Without one, the seed of the fit is used.

Value

diagnose_confusion() returns an object of class diagnose_confusion, a list with the mean confusion_matrix, its confusion_matrix_sd, confusion_matrix_ci_lower, and confusion_matrix_ci_upper, the metrics, the threshold_confusion_matrix, the roc curve, and the auc. tidy() returns a tibble of threshold, fpr, and tpr, and glance() a tibble of one row of the metrics. print() returns x, invisibly.

Details

The predicted probabilities are those of the observed model, which the permutations do not change. A linear probability model can predict a value below 0 or above 1, which is taken as 0 or 1.

estimate_mrqap() keeps the result for a binary outcome as $confusion_matrix, from 1000 draws with the seed of the fit.

See also

Other models: control_mrqap(), other_results, play_diffusions(), print.netreg_lm(), regression, specify, specify_terms, terms_mrqap, test_fit, test_measures, test_parameter()

Examples

fit <- estimate_mrqap(. ~ ego(Age) + alter(Age),
                      manynet::ison_adolescents |>
                        manynet::mutate_nodes(Age = 12:19),
                      times = 20, control = list(seed = 1))
(conf <- diagnose_confusion(fit))
#> # Confusion matrix of a logistic MRQAP of ties
#> # From 1000 draws of the predicted probabilities, with 95% intervals
#> 
#>       Predicted
#> Actual 0             1         
#>      0 13.6 [11, 16] 4.5 [2, 7]
#>      1 4.4 [2, 7]    5.5 [3, 8]
#> 
#>  accuracy sensitivity specificity precision    f1   auc threshold
#>     0.682       0.554       0.753      0.56 0.551 0.822       0.5
#>  threshold.accuracy nobs draws
#>               0.786   28  1000
glance(conf)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 10
#>   accuracy sensitivity specificity precision    f1   auc threshold
#>      <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1    0.682       0.554       0.753     0.560 0.551 0.822       0.5
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: threshold.accuracy <dbl>, nobs <int>, draws <int>
tidy(conf)
#> # A tibble: 29 × 3
#>    threshold    fpr   tpr
#>        <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1   Inf     0        0  
#>  2     0.843 0        0.1
#>  3     0.808 0        0.2
#>  4     0.768 0        0.3
#>  5     0.722 0        0.4
#>  6     0.671 0.0556   0.4
#>  7     0.641 0.111    0.4
#>  8     0.616 0.111    0.5
#>  9     0.584 0.167    0.5
#> 10     0.557 0.167    0.6
#> # ℹ 19 more rows
